mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising real discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 below -2% signals a contraction in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered GDP contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for two consecutive months indicates weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in RSAFS (consumer savings) by more than 1% signals a tightening monetary environment with reduced household liquidity, which depresses consumer spending and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand for goods and housing, which reduces corporate revenues and equity multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between PAYEMS growth and S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exists during a late-cycle expansion, as rising employment signals robust demand and earnings growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly PAYEMS growth and subsequent 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) during a defined late-cycle window.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL rises above 3% for three consecutive months while FEDFUNDS remains below 2%, it signals accommodative policy lagging inflation, eroding real purchasing power and compressing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: inflation surprise with loose monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of such co-triggered episodes.
